chapters.1.summary: This short poem opens the book of Psalms. It calls a person blessed who stays away from the advice of the wicked. That person delights in the LORD’s teaching and thinks on it day and night. He is like a tree planted beside streams. The wicked are like chaff that the wind blows away. They will not stand in the judgment. The LORD knows the way of the righteous, and the way of the wicked ends.
chapters.2.summary: Nations and kings plot against the LORD and his anointed king. The one enthroned in heaven laughs at them. He says he has set his king on Zion, his holy hill. The king reports God’s decree: “You are my son.” The nations are promised to him as an inheritance. The poem then warns the kings of the earth to be wise. They should serve the LORD with fear. All who take refuge in him are blessed.
chapters.3.summary: The heading sets this prayer in David’s flight from his son Absalom. The speaker says his enemies are many. Many say God will not help him. He answers that the LORD is a shield around him. He cried out, and the LORD answered from his holy hill. He lay down, slept, and woke again. He will not fear ten thousand people set against him. He asks the LORD to rise and save.
chapters.4.summary: The speaker asks God to answer when he calls. He asks people how long they will love empty things and lies. He says the LORD has set apart the faithful for himself. He tells them to tremble, search their hearts in bed, and be still. Many ask who will show them any good. The speaker asks for the light of God’s face. He has more joy than others have at harvest. He lies down and sleeps in peace.
chapters.5.summary: The speaker asks the LORD to hear his words and his sighing. He prays in the morning and watches for an answer. God takes no pleasure in wickedness, and the proud cannot stand before him. The LORD hates liars and violent men. The speaker will enter God’s house through great kindness. He asks to be led on a straight path because of his enemies. Their throats are open graves. He asks that all who take refuge in God may rejoice.
chapters.6.summary: The speaker asks the LORD not to rebuke him in anger. He is faint, and his bones are troubled. He asks how long and cannot finish the sentence. He asks to be saved for the sake of God’s kindness. No one praises God from the grave. He floods his bed with tears every night. Then he orders the evildoers to leave. The LORD has heard the sound of his weeping.
chapters.7.summary: The heading says David sang this about the words of Cush the Benjamite. The speaker takes refuge in the LORD and fears being torn as by a lion. He swears that if he has wronged a friend, his enemy may crush him. He asks the LORD to rise and judge the peoples. He asks to be judged by his own right conduct. God tests hearts and minds. The one who digs a pit falls into it. The speaker gives thanks for the LORD’s justice.
chapters.8.summary: The poem begins and ends by praising the LORD’s majestic name. His glory is above the heavens. Even the mouths of infants serve as his strength. The speaker looks at the moon and the stars. He asks what a human being is that God should care. Yet God made humans a little lower than the heavenly beings. He crowned them with glory and honor. He put flocks, wild animals, birds, and fish under their care.
chapters.9.summary: The speaker thanks the LORD with his whole heart. His enemies fell back when God judged from the throne. The LORD rules forever and judges the world rightly. He is a high tower for the oppressed. He does not forget the cry of the afflicted. The speaker asks to be lifted from the gates of death. Nations sink in the pit they dug. He asks God to let the nations know they are only human.
chapters.10.summary: The speaker asks why the LORD stands far off in times of trouble. A proud man hunts the poor. He says in his heart that there is no God to call him to account. His ways prosper, and he thinks nothing can shake him. He waits in ambush in the villages and seizes the helpless. The speaker asks God to rise and lift his hand. He says God does see trouble and grief. The LORD hears the humble and defends the orphan.
chapters.11.summary: The speaker has taken refuge in the LORD. Friends tell him to flee like a bird to the mountains. The wicked have bent their bows to shoot from the dark. If the foundations are destroyed, they ask, what can the righteous do? The speaker answers that the LORD is in his holy temple. His throne is in heaven, and his eyes examine everyone. He tests the righteous and hates violence. The upright will see his face.
chapters.12.summary: The speaker cries for help because faithful people have vanished. Everyone lies to his neighbor with flattering lips. The proud say their tongues will win and no one rules them. The LORD answers that he will now rise. He acts because the weak are oppressed and the needy groan. The LORD’s words are pure, like silver refined seven times. He will guard the poor. Still the wicked strut about when vileness is honored.
chapters.13.summary: The speaker asks the LORD four times, “How long?” He asks whether God will forget him forever. He has sorrow in his heart every day. His enemy is winning. He asks God to look, answer, and give light to his eyes. Otherwise he will sleep in death. Then he says he trusts in God’s kindness. He will sing, because the LORD has been good to him.
chapters.14.summary: The fool says in his heart that there is no God. People are corrupt, and no one does good. The LORD looks down from heaven to see whether anyone seeks him. All have turned aside. Evildoers eat up God’s people as they eat bread. They do not call on the LORD. Yet God is with the righteous, and he is the refuge of the poor. The speaker longs for Israel’s rescue to come from Zion.
chapters.15.summary: The poem asks who may stay in the LORD’s tent and on his holy hill. The answer is a person who lives blamelessly and does right. He speaks truth in his heart. He does not slander or harm a friend. He honors those who fear the LORD. He keeps an oath even when it costs him. He lends without interest and takes no bribe. Such a person will never be shaken.
chapters.16.summary: The speaker asks God to keep him, for he takes refuge in him. He has no good apart from the LORD. Those who chase other gods multiply their sorrows. The LORD is his portion and his cup. The boundary lines have fallen for him in pleasant places. He blesses the LORD, who counsels him even at night. His body will rest secure. God will show him the path of life and lasting joy.
chapters.17.summary: The speaker asks the LORD to hear a just cause from honest lips. God has tested his heart by night and found no plan to do wrong. He has kept away from violent paths. He asks God to show his wonderful kindness. He asks to be kept as the apple of the eye. Enemies surround him like a lion hungry for prey. Their reward is in this life only. He expects to see God’s face when he wakes.
chapters.18.summary: The speaker loves the LORD, his rock and fortress. The cords of death once wrapped around him, and he cried out. The earth shook, and God came down in smoke, fire, and storm. He reached from on high and drew the speaker out of deep waters. He brought him into a wide place. God lights his lamp and trains his hands for battle. With God’s help he overcomes his enemies. He praises the LORD, who shows kindness to David and his line.
chapters.19.summary: The heavens tell God’s glory without speech or words. Their message goes out through all the earth. The sun runs its course like a strong man, and nothing hides from its heat. The LORD’s law is perfect and restores the soul. His commands are right, pure, and sweeter than honey. The speaker asks who can see his own errors. He asks to be cleared of hidden faults. He prays that his words and thoughts will please the LORD.
chapters.20.summary: The people pray for their king before a battle. They ask the LORD to answer him in the day of trouble. They ask God to send help from the sanctuary and remember his offerings. They will shout for joy at his victory. A single voice says the LORD saves his anointed. Some trust in chariots and horses. The people trust in the name of the LORD. They ask the King to answer when they call.
chapters.21.summary: The king rejoices in the LORD’s strength. God has given him his heart’s desire. God set a crown of fine gold on his head. He asked for life, and God gave it. His glory is great because God saved him. The king trusts in the LORD and will not be shaken. God’s hand will find all his enemies. The people sing and praise God’s power.
chapters.22.summary: The speaker cries, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” He calls day and night and gets no answer. He recalls that his fathers trusted God and were rescued. People mock him and shake their heads. He is poured out like water, and his bones are out of joint. Men stare at him and cast lots for his clothing. He begs God not to be far away. Then he praises God, and the ends of the earth turn to the LORD.
chapters.23.lds: Come, Follow Me uses the shepherd image to study Christ’s care. What does the host provide in verse 5?
chapters.23.summary: The speaker says the LORD is his shepherd, so he lacks nothing. The shepherd leads him to green pastures and still waters. He restores his soul and guides him in right paths. Even in the darkest valley the speaker fears no evil. God’s rod and staff comfort him. God prepares a table for him in front of his enemies. God anoints his head with oil, and his cup overflows. Goodness and kindness will follow him all his life.
chapters.24.summary: The earth and everything in it belong to the LORD. He founded it on the seas. The poem asks who may go up the LORD’s hill and stand there. The answer is one with clean hands and a pure heart. That person does not trust in lies or swear falsely. Then the gates are told to lift up their heads. The King of glory is coming in. He is the LORD of Armies, strong and mighty in battle.
chapters.25.summary: The speaker lifts his soul to the LORD and asks not to be shamed. He asks God to show him his ways and teach him his paths. He asks God to remember mercy and not the sins of his youth. The LORD is good and teaches sinners the way. The speaker asks pardon for his guilt, which is great. He is lonely and afflicted. The troubles of his heart have grown. He asks God to guard his life and redeem Israel.
chapters.26.summary: The speaker asks the LORD to judge him, since he has walked in integrity. He invites God to test his heart and mind. He keeps God’s kindness before his eyes. He does not sit with deceitful people. He washes his hands in innocence and walks around the altar. He sings thanks and loves the house where God’s glory lives. He asks not to be swept away with men who take bribes. He asks to be redeemed and shown mercy.
chapters.27.summary: The LORD is the speaker’s light and salvation, so he fears no one. Even if an army camps against him, he will be confident. He has asked one thing: to live in the LORD’s house and see his beauty. God will hide him in his shelter in the day of trouble. Then the tone changes, and he begs God to hear him. He asks God not to hide his face or abandon him. False witnesses have risen against him. He tells himself to wait for the LORD and be strong.
chapters.28.summary: The speaker calls to the LORD, his rock, and asks him not to be deaf. If God is silent, he will be like those who go down to the pit. He lifts his hands toward the holy place. He asks not to be dragged off with the wicked. They speak peace to neighbors with harm in their hearts. Then he blesses the LORD for hearing his cry. The LORD is his strength and shield. He asks God to save his people and carry them forever.
chapters.29.summary: The poem calls the heavenly beings to give the LORD glory. The LORD’s voice sounds over the waters and thunders. His voice breaks the cedars of Lebanon. It makes the mountains skip like a calf. It strikes with flashes of fire and shakes the wilderness. It strips the forests bare. In his temple everyone says, “Glory!” The LORD sits as king forever and blesses his people with peace.
chapters.30.summary: The speaker praises the LORD for lifting him up. He cried for help, and God healed him and kept him from the grave. God’s anger lasts a moment, and his favor a lifetime. Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning. In good times the speaker said he would never be shaken. Then God hid his face, and he was terrified. He pleaded for his life. God turned his mourning into dancing and clothed him with gladness.
chapters.31.summary: The speaker takes refuge in the LORD and asks for quick rescue. He commits his spirit into God’s hand. He is in distress, and grief wastes his eyes and body. Neighbors dread him, and he is forgotten like a dead man. He hears whispering and plots against his life. Yet he says, “You are my God,” and that his times are in God’s hand. He praises the goodness God stores up for those who fear him. He tells all who hope in the LORD to be strong.
chapters.32.summary: The speaker calls a person blessed whose sin is forgiven and covered. While he kept silent, his bones wasted away. God’s hand was heavy on him day and night. His strength dried up as in summer heat. Then he admitted his sin and did not hide it. God forgave him. So the faithful should pray while God may be found. He tells others not to be like a mule that needs bit and bridle.
chapters.33.summary: The poem calls the righteous to praise the LORD with lyre and harp. The LORD’s word is right, and the earth is full of his kindness. By his word the heavens were made. He spoke, and it was done. He overturns the plans of nations, and his own plan stands. He looks from heaven and sees every person. No king is saved by a great army. The LORD’s eye is on those who hope in his kindness.
chapters.34.summary: The heading says David acted insane before Abimelech, who sent him away. The speaker blesses the LORD, who answered him and freed him from his fears. He calls himself a poor man who cried and was heard. He invites others to taste and see that the LORD is good. He then teaches the young to fear the LORD. They should keep their tongues from evil and seek peace. The LORD is near the brokenhearted. The righteous have many troubles, and the LORD rescues them from all.
chapters.35.summary: The speaker asks the LORD to fight those who fight him. Without cause they hid a net for him. False witnesses accuse him and repay his good with evil. When they were sick, he wore sackcloth and fasted for them. He grieved as for a friend, a brother, or a mother. When he stumbled, they gathered to mock and tear at him. He asks how long God will look on. He promises thanks in the great assembly.
chapters.36.summary: The poem begins inside the mind of a wicked man. He has no fear of God and flatters himself. He plots harm even on his bed. Then the poem turns to the LORD’s kindness, which reaches the heavens. His justice is like the great mountains and the deep sea. He preserves both people and animals. People take refuge under his wings and drink from his river of delights. With him is the fountain of life.
chapters.37.summary: This poem teaches like a proverb collection. It says not to fret over evildoers, who wither like grass. Trust the LORD, do good, and wait for him. Anger leads only to doing wrong. The humble will inherit the land. The LORD holds the hand of the one who stumbles. The speaker is old and has not seen the righteous abandoned. The wicked flourish like a green tree and then are gone.
chapters.38.summary: The speaker asks the LORD not to punish him in anger. God’s arrows have sunk into him. His body has no health, and he links this to his sin. His wounds fester, and he is bent over all day. His heart pounds, and his strength fails. Friends and neighbors keep their distance. Enemies set traps and talk of ruin. He stays silent, waits for the LORD, and asks him to hurry.
chapters.39.summary: The heading names Jeduthun. The speaker resolved to guard his mouth while the wicked were near. He kept silent, and his pain grew until his heart burned and he spoke. He asks the LORD to show him how short his life is. His days are a few handbreadths, and every person is a breath. People heap up wealth and do not know who will get it. His hope is in the LORD. He asks God to hear his tears, for he is a passing guest.
chapters.40.summary: The speaker waited for the LORD, who heard his cry. God lifted him from a muddy pit and set his feet on rock. God put a new song in his mouth. God did not want sacrifice but an open ear. The speaker says he delights to do God’s will. He has told the great assembly of God’s faithfulness. Now troubles without number surround him again. He is poor and needy and asks God not to delay.
chapters.41.summary: The poem blesses the one who cares for the weak. The LORD sustains such a person on a sickbed. The speaker is ill and asks for mercy, since he has sinned. His enemies ask when he will die. Visitors speak empty words and gather gossip to spread. Even his close friend, who ate his bread, has turned against him. He asks God to raise him up. A blessing on the LORD closes this first part of the Psalms.
chapters.42.summary: The speaker thirsts for God as a deer pants for streams. Tears are his food while people ask where his God is. He remembers leading the crowd to God’s house with joyful songs. He asks his own soul why it is in despair. He tells it to hope in God. He is far away in the north, near Mount Hermon. Waves and breakers have gone over him. He asks God, his rock, why he has been forgotten.
chapters.43.summary: The speaker asks God to defend him against unjust and deceitful people. God is his strength, yet he feels rejected. He asks why he must go about mourning. He asks God to send out light and truth. They will lead him to God’s holy hill. Then he will go to the altar of God, his great joy. He will praise God with the harp. He again tells his soul to hope in God.
chapters.44.summary: The people have heard from their fathers what God did long ago. He drove out nations and planted Israel, and their own swords did not do it. They still boast in God all day. Yet now he has rejected them and let them be defeated. They are scattered and mocked by their neighbors. All this has happened, though they have not forgotten him. They have not been false to his covenant. They cry for him to wake up and help.
chapters.45.summary: This is a song for a king’s wedding. The poet’s heart overflows, and his tongue is like a skilled writer’s pen. He praises the king’s beauty and gracious speech. The king should ride out for truth, humility, and right. His throne lasts, and he loves what is right. His robes smell of myrrh, and music comes from ivory palaces. The poet tells the bride to forget her people and her father’s house. She is led to the king in embroidered robes with her companions.
chapters.46.summary: God is the people’s refuge and strength, a help found in trouble. They will not fear though the earth gives way. Mountains may fall into the sea, and waters may roar. A river makes God’s city glad, and God is in the middle of it. Nations rage, and kingdoms totter. God speaks, and the earth melts. He ends wars, breaks the bow, and burns the chariots. He says, “Be still, and know that I am God.”
chapters.47.summary: The poem calls all peoples to clap and shout to God. The LORD Most High is a great king over all the earth. He chose an inheritance for Jacob, whom he loves. God has gone up with a shout and the sound of a trumpet. The people are told five times to sing praises. God reigns over the nations and sits on his holy throne. The princes of the peoples gather with the people of Abraham’s God.
chapters.48.summary: The LORD is great in the city of our God. Mount Zion is beautiful and is the joy of the whole earth. God has made himself known in her fortresses as a refuge. Kings gathered against her, saw her, and fled in panic. The people have heard of this, and now they have seen it. They think about God’s kindness inside his temple. They are told to walk around Zion and count her towers. They must tell the next generation that this God is their God.
chapters.49.summary: The poet calls all people to listen, low and high, rich and poor. He will speak wisdom and explain a riddle with the harp. He asks why he should fear when the wealthy surround him. No one can pay God a ransom for another person’s life. The wise and the foolish die alike and leave their wealth. Their graves are their homes, though they named lands after themselves. Death is their shepherd. But God will redeem the speaker’s life from the grave.
chapters.50.summary: The heading names Asaph. God, the LORD, calls heaven and earth as witnesses while he judges his people. He does not fault their sacrifices. But he needs no bull from their stalls, since every animal is his. If he were hungry, he would not tell them. He asks for thanks, kept vows, and prayer in trouble. He rebukes the wicked who recite his laws and join with thieves. They thought he was like them, because he kept silent.
chapters.51.summary: The heading sets this prayer after Nathan confronted David about Bathsheba. The speaker asks God for mercy and to blot out his wrongs. He knows his sin, and it is always before him. He asks to be washed whiter than snow. He asks God to create a clean heart in him. He asks not to be cast from God’s presence. Then he will teach other wrongdoers God’s ways. God wants a broken and humble heart more than a burnt offering.
chapters.52.summary: The heading names Doeg, who told Saul that David went to Ahimelech’s house. The speaker asks a powerful man why he boasts of evil. His tongue is like a sharp razor and loves lies. God will tear him from his tent and uproot him from the living. The righteous will see it and laugh. That man trusted his great wealth and not God. The speaker is like a green olive tree in God’s house. He trusts God’s kindness and gives thanks.
chapters.53.summary: This poem is nearly the same as Psalm 14. The fool says in his heart that there is no God. People are corrupt, and no one does good. God looks down to see whether anyone seeks him. Everyone has turned away. Evildoers eat up God’s people like bread and never call on him. Then great terror falls on them where no terror was. The speaker longs for Israel’s rescue to come from Zion.
chapters.54.summary: The heading says men of Ziph told Saul where David was hiding. The speaker asks God to save him by his name. Strangers have risen against him, and violent men want his life. They do not keep God before them. Then he says that God is his helper. The Lord sustains his life. He will bring a freewill offering and give thanks. God has rescued him from every trouble.
chapters.55.summary: The speaker asks God not to hide from his plea. His heart is in anguish, and the terrors of death have fallen on him. He wishes for a dove’s wings to fly away and rest. He sees violence, strife, and fraud in the city. An enemy’s insult he could have borne. But this was his equal, his companion and close friend. They used to walk together to God’s house. He tells himself to cast his burden on the LORD.
chapters.56.summary: The heading says the Philistines seized David in Gath. The speaker asks for mercy, since men attack him all day. When he is afraid, he puts his trust in God. He asks what mere flesh can do to him. His enemies twist his words and watch his steps. He says God has counted his wanderings. God keeps his tears in a bottle and writes them in a book. He knows that God is for him.
chapters.57.summary: The heading sets this prayer in the cave where David hid from Saul. The speaker asks for mercy and shelters under God’s wings. He will stay there until the danger passes. He lies among lions whose teeth are spears. He asks God to be exalted above the heavens. His enemies dug a pit and fell into it themselves. His heart is steady, and he will sing. He will wake the dawn with harp and lyre.
chapters.58.summary: The speaker asks rulers whether they really speak justice. He says their hearts plan wrong and their hands deal out violence. The wicked go astray from birth. Their poison is like a cobra’s that hears no charmer. He asks God to break their teeth. He asks that they vanish like water that runs off. The righteous will be glad when they see justice done. People will say there is a God who judges the earth.
chapters.59.summary: The heading says Saul sent men to watch David’s house and kill him. The speaker asks God to rescue him from men who lie in wait. He has done no wrong to them. They return at evening, howl like dogs, and prowl the city. They think no one hears. The LORD laughs at them. The speaker asks God to scatter them but not to kill them. In the morning he will sing of God’s strength.
chapters.60.summary: The heading sets this prayer when David fought Aram and Joab struck Edom. The people say God has rejected them and broken their defenses. He has shaken the land and made them stagger. They ask him to save with his right hand. God has spoken: Shechem, Gilead, Ephraim, and Judah are his. Moab, Edom, and Philistia are under him. Yet God has not gone out with their armies. They ask for his help, since human help is worthless.
chapters.61.summary: The speaker asks God to hear his cry. He calls from the end of the earth with a fainting heart. He asks to be led to a rock higher than himself. God has been his refuge and a strong tower. He wants to live in God’s tent and shelter under his wings. God has heard his vows. He prays for long life for the king. He will sing and keep his vows day after day.
chapters.62.summary: The heading names Jeduthun. The speaker waits in silence for God alone, his rock and fortress. Men attack him like a leaning wall and bless with their mouths while cursing inside. He tells his soul again to wait. He tells the people to trust God and pour out their hearts. Human beings of every rank weigh less than a breath. They should not trust in extortion or set their hearts on wealth. Power and kindness both belong to God.
chapters.63.summary: The heading sets this prayer in the wilderness of Judah. The speaker thirsts for God in a dry and weary land. He has seen God’s power in the sanctuary. God’s kindness is better than life. His soul is satisfied as with the richest food. He remembers God on his bed through the night watches. He clings to God, whose right hand holds him. Those who seek his life will fall, and the king will rejoice.
chapters.64.summary: The speaker asks God to hear his complaint and guard his life. The wicked plot in secret. They sharpen their tongues like swords and aim bitter words like arrows. They shoot from hiding at the innocent. They encourage one another and ask who will see them. God will shoot his own arrow at them suddenly. Their own tongues will bring them down. Everyone will fear and tell what God has done.
chapters.65.summary: Praise waits for God in Zion. He hears prayer, and all people come to him. He forgives the sins that overwhelm them. He set the mountains in place and stills the roaring seas. He visits the earth and waters it. He drenches the furrows and softens the ground with showers. He crowns the year with goodness. The pastures and valleys are covered with flocks and grain, and they sing.
chapters.66.summary: The poem calls all the earth to shout to God. People are invited to come and see what he has done. He turned the sea into dry land. He tested his people and refined them like silver. They went through fire and water, and he brought them to a rich place. Then one voice speaks. He will pay the vows he made in distress. He tells all who fear God what God has done for him.
chapters.67.summary: The people ask God to be merciful, bless them, and shine his face on them. They ask this so that his way may be known on earth. All nations should know his salvation. The peoples are called to praise God and be glad. He judges them fairly and guides them. The earth has given its harvest. God blesses his people, and all the ends of the earth will fear him.
chapters.68.summary: God rises, and his enemies scatter like smoke. The righteous sing to the one who rides through the deserts. He is a father to orphans and a defender of widows. He gives the lonely a home and leads prisoners out. He marched before his people, and Sinai shook. Kings and armies flee. A procession of singers, musicians, and young women enters the sanctuary. Kings bring gifts, and God gives strength to his people.
chapters.69.summary: The speaker cries that the waters have reached his neck. He sinks in deep mud, and his throat is dry from calling. Many hate him without cause. He bears insult for God’s sake and is a stranger to his brothers. People at the gate talk about him, and drunkards sing about him. Insult has broken his heart. He looked for pity and found none. He asks God to answer, and he promises a song of thanks.
chapters.70.summary: This short prayer asks God to hurry. The speaker wants those who seek his life to be put to shame. He wants those who mock him turned back. He wants all who seek God to rejoice and say that God is great. He is poor and needy. He asks God to come quickly. God is his help and rescuer, and he asks him not to delay.
chapters.71.summary: The speaker takes refuge in the LORD and asks for rescue. God has been his hope since his youth. He has leaned on God from birth. He asks not to be cast off in old age when his strength fails. His enemies say God has left him. He will still hope and tell of God’s saving acts all day. He asks to live until he has told the next generation. He will praise God with harp and lyre.
chapters.72.summary: This is a prayer for the king. The people ask God to give him justice. He should defend the poor, save needy children, and crush the oppressor. May he be like rain on a mown field. May he rule from sea to sea and receive gifts from distant kings. He rescues the needy who cry out and have no helper. Their blood is precious to him. May all nations be blessed through him.
chapters.73.summary: The heading names Asaph. The speaker says God is good to the pure in heart. Yet his feet almost slipped when he envied the arrogant and saw them prosper. They have no pain, wear pride like a necklace, and mock heaven. He wondered whether he had kept his heart clean for nothing. The problem wore him out until he entered God’s sanctuary. There he understood their end. He says God holds his hand and is his portion forever.
chapters.74.summary: The heading names Asaph. The people ask God why he has rejected them. Enemies have ruined everything in the sanctuary. They hacked the carved wood with axes and burned the holy place. They burned every meeting place in the land. No signs are seen, no prophet remains, and no one knows how long. The people recall that God divided the sea and crushed the sea monsters. They ask him to remember his covenant and defend his cause.
chapters.75.summary: The heading names Asaph. The people thank God, whose name is near. God says he will judge at his chosen time and holds the earth’s pillars steady. He tells the proud not to boast or lift up their strength. Honor does not come from east, west, or the desert. God is the judge, who puts one down and lifts another up. He holds a cup of foaming wine for the wicked. The speaker will sing praise to the God of Jacob.
chapters.76.summary: The heading names Asaph. God is known in Judah, and his dwelling is in Zion. There he broke the flaming arrows, the shield, and the sword. Brave soldiers lay stunned, and at his rebuke horse and chariot fell still. No one can stand when he is angry. The earth feared and was quiet when God rose to judge. He rose to save all the afflicted of the earth. Rulers should bring gifts to the one who humbles princes.
chapters.77.summary: The heading names Asaph and Jeduthun. The speaker cries aloud to God in the day of trouble. At night he finds no comfort, and he cannot sleep or speak. He asks whether the Lord will reject forever and whether his kindness has ended. Then he decides to remember the LORD’s deeds of old. God redeemed the children of Jacob and Joseph. The waters saw him and trembled. He led his people through the sea like a flock.
chapters.78.summary: The heading names Asaph. The poet asks the people to listen, for fathers must tell children the LORD’s deeds. Then each generation will hope in God and not be stubborn. He recalls the sea, the cloud, water from the rock, and manna. The people still tested God and forgot his works. God was merciful and remembered that they were only flesh. He left Shiloh and let the ark be captured. He chose Judah, Mount Zion, and David the shepherd.
chapters.79.summary: The heading names Asaph. The nations have invaded God’s land, defiled his temple, and left Jerusalem in ruins. The bodies of God’s servants are left for birds and animals. Neighbors mock the survivors. The people ask how long God will be angry. They ask him not to hold their earlier sins against them. They ask for help and forgiveness for the sake of his name. Then his people, his flock, will thank him forever.
chapters.80.summary: The heading names Asaph. The people call on the Shepherd of Israel to shine and save them. Three times they ask God to restore them and let his face shine. He has fed them with tears. They recall that God brought a vine out of Egypt and planted it. It filled the land and shaded the mountains. Now its walls are broken, passersby pick its fruit, and a wild boar tears it. They ask God to look down and care for this vine.
chapters.81.summary: The heading names Asaph. The poem opens with a call to sing and play at the festival. Trumpets sound at the new moon, as Israel’s law requires, and then God speaks. He lifted the burden from Israel’s shoulder in Egypt. He tells his people to have no foreign god. He brought them out of Egypt and will fill their open mouths. But the people would not listen, so he let them follow their own plans. If they would listen, he would feed them with the finest wheat.
chapters.82.summary: The heading names Asaph. God stands in the assembly and judges among the “gods.” He asks how long they will judge unjustly and favor the wicked. He orders them to defend the weak and the fatherless. They must rescue the poor from the wicked. They walk in darkness, and the earth’s foundations shake. God says they will die like men. The poet asks God to rise and judge the earth, since all nations are his.
chapters.83.summary: The heading names Asaph. The people ask God not to stay silent. Enemies are plotting to wipe out Israel’s name. Ten peoples have joined together, from Edom and Moab to Tyre and Assyria. The people ask God to treat them as he treated Midian and Sisera. They ask that the enemies be like windblown dust and their faces filled with shame. Then they may seek his name. Let them know that the LORD alone is Most High.
chapters.84.summary: The speaker loves the LORD’s dwelling and longs for its courts. Even the sparrow and the swallow have nests near God’s altars. Those who live in God’s house are blessed. So are those who set their hearts on the road to Zion. They pass through a dry valley and make it a place of springs. A day in God’s courts is better than a thousand elsewhere. The speaker would choose to be a doorkeeper there. The LORD is a sun and shield.
chapters.85.summary: The people recall that the LORD once restored and forgave them. They ask him to restore them again. They ask whether he will be angry forever. The speaker will listen for what God says. God speaks peace to his people, and they must not return to folly. Mercy and truth meet. Righteousness and peace kiss each other. The LORD will give what is good, and the land will yield its harvest.
chapters.86.summary: The speaker is poor and needy and asks the LORD to hear him. God is good, forgiving, and full of kindness to all who call. No god is like him. All nations he made will come and worship. The speaker asks to be taught God’s way. He asks for an undivided heart. Proud and violent men seek his life. He calls God merciful and gracious and asks for a sign of favor.
chapters.87.summary: The LORD loves the gates of Zion, and glorious things are said of the city. God lists nations among those who know him. He names Egypt, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia. Of each one it is said, “This one was born there.” The Most High himself will establish Zion. When he registers the peoples, he records them as born in her. Singers and dancers say all their springs are in her.
chapters.88.summary: The heading names the sons of Korah and Heman the Ezrahite. The speaker cries to the LORD day and night. His life is full of trouble and close to the grave. He is counted among the dead whom God remembers no more. God’s anger lies heavy on him. He asks whether God works wonders for the dead. He has been afflicted since his youth. Friend and neighbor are gone, and darkness is his companion.
chapters.89.summary: The heading names Ethan the Ezrahite. The poet sings of the LORD’s kindness and faithfulness. God swore that David’s line and throne would last forever. The heavens praise him, and justice is the base of his throne. If David’s sons sin, God will punish them and still keep his kindness. Then the poem turns. God has rejected his anointed and thrown the crown in the dust. Walls are broken, enemies rejoice, and the poet asks where the former kindness is.
chapters.90.summary: The heading calls this a prayer of Moses. The Lord has been his people’s home in every generation. He was God before the mountains were born. A thousand years are like a day to him. People are like grass that sprouts in the morning and withers by evening. A life lasts seventy or eighty years and is full of toil. The speaker asks God to teach them to count their days. He asks God to establish the work of their hands.
chapters.91.summary: The poem speaks of one who lives in the shelter of the Most High. God will save him from the hunter’s trap and from deadly disease. He covers him with his feathers. He need not fear terror by night or arrows by day. Angels will guard him and lift him up. Then God speaks. He will rescue the one who loves him and answer when he calls. He will be with him in trouble and give him long life.
chapters.92.summary: The heading calls this a song for the Sabbath day. It is good to thank the LORD with harp and lyre. His works make the speaker glad, and his thoughts are deep. A senseless person does not understand this. The wicked sprout like grass and are destroyed forever. The righteous flourish like a palm and grow like a cedar. They are planted in the LORD’s house. They still bear fruit in old age.
chapters.93.summary: The LORD reigns and is robed in majesty. He has made the world firm, and it cannot be moved. His throne was set up long ago. The floods have lifted up their voice and their pounding waves. The LORD on high is mightier than the thunder of many waters. His decrees are very sure. Holiness belongs to his house forever.
chapters.94.summary: The speaker calls on God to rise as judge of the earth. The wicked crush God’s people. They kill the widow, the foreigner, and the orphan. They say the LORD does not see. The speaker answers that the maker of the ear can hear. The LORD will not abandon his people. When the speaker’s foot slipped, God’s kindness held him up. He asks whether a wicked throne that makes harm legal can be God’s ally.
chapters.95.summary: The poem invites the people to sing to the LORD, their rock. He is a great King above all gods. The depths, the mountains, and the sea are his. They are called to kneel before their Maker. They are the sheep of his hand. Then a warning comes: hear his voice today. Do not harden your hearts as at Meribah in the wilderness. That generation tested God and did not enter his rest.
chapters.96.summary: The poem calls all the earth to sing a new song to the LORD. His glory should be told among the nations. The gods of the peoples are idols, but the LORD made the heavens. Families of nations should bring him an offering. They should say that the LORD reigns and judges fairly. The heavens, the earth, and the sea are called to rejoice. The fields and the trees of the forest sing. He is coming to judge the earth with justice.
chapters.97.summary: The LORD reigns, and the earth should be glad. Clouds and darkness surround him. Justice is the base of his throne. Fire goes before him, and the mountains melt like wax. The heavens declare his justice. All who worship idols are put to shame. Those who love the LORD must hate evil. Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the honest in heart.
chapters.98.summary: The poem calls for a new song, since the LORD has done wonderful things. His right hand has won the victory. He has shown his saving power to the nations. He remembered his kindness to Israel. All the earth should shout with lyre, trumpets, and horn. The sea should roar, and the rivers clap their hands. The mountains should sing together. The LORD is coming to judge the world fairly.
chapters.99.summary: The LORD reigns, and the peoples tremble. He sits enthroned above the cherubim. He is holy. The King loves justice and has established fairness in Israel. Moses, Aaron, and Samuel called on him, and he answered. He spoke to them from the pillar of cloud. He forgave them, and he also punished their wrongs. The people are called to worship at his holy hill.
chapters.100.summary: This short psalm of thanks calls all lands to shout to the LORD. They should serve him with gladness and come with singing. They should know that the LORD is God. He made them, and they are his. They are his people and the sheep of his pasture. They should enter his gates with thanks and his courts with praise. The LORD is good. His kindness lasts forever, and his faithfulness reaches every generation.
chapters.101.summary: A ruler sings of kindness and justice. He promises to live with a blameless heart inside his own house. He will set nothing worthless before his eyes. He will silence anyone who slanders a neighbor in secret. He will not put up with proud looks. He will look for faithful people to live with him and serve him. No liar will stay in his house. Each morning he will remove the wicked from the LORD’s city.
chapters.102.summary: The heading calls this the prayer of a suffering person who is faint. His days vanish like smoke, and his heart is withered like grass. He is like a lonely bird on a roof. His enemies mock him, and he eats ashes with his bread. Yet the LORD sits enthroned forever. He will rise and have mercy on Zion. This will be written for a generation still to come. The heavens will wear out like clothing, but God stays the same.
chapters.103.summary: The speaker tells his soul to bless the LORD and forget none of his gifts. God forgives, heals, and rescues his life from the pit. He is merciful and gracious and slow to anger. He does not treat people as their sins deserve. His kindness is as high as the heavens are above the earth. He pities his children as a father does. He remembers that people are dust. Human life is like grass, but his kindness lasts forever.
chapters.104.summary: The speaker blesses the LORD, who is clothed with light. God stretched out the heavens and set the earth on its foundations. He sends springs into the valleys for the wild animals. He grows grass for cattle and plants, wine, oil, and bread for people. Lions hunt at night, and people work by day. The sea holds creatures beyond number. All of them wait for God to give their food. He takes their breath, and they die; he sends his Spirit, and they are created.
chapters.105.summary: The poem calls the people to remember the LORD’s wonders. He made a covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and promised them a land. When they were few, he protected them. He sent Joseph ahead as a slave, and Joseph rose to rule Egypt. Israel grew there and was hated. God sent Moses, Aaron, and the plagues. He brought his people out with joy and fed them in the desert. He gave them lands so that they would keep his laws.
chapters.106.summary: The poem begins with praise and a prayer to be remembered. Then it confesses: we have sinned as our fathers did. The fathers forgot God’s wonders at the Red Sea. They craved food in the desert and envied Moses. They made a calf at Horeb, and Moses stood in the gap for them. They joined in the worship of Baal and later sacrificed their children. God gave them over to the nations many times. Yet he heard their cry and remembered his covenant.
chapters.107.summary: The poem calls the redeemed to thank the LORD. It describes four groups in trouble. Some wandered hungry in the desert. Some sat in dark prisons because they had rebelled. Some were sick through their own folly. Some were caught in a storm at sea. Each group cried to the LORD, and he rescued them. He turns rivers into desert and desert into pools, and the wise will consider this.
chapters.108.summary: The speaker’s heart is steady, and he will sing and wake the dawn. He will give thanks among the nations. God’s kindness is higher than the heavens. He asks God to save with his right hand. God has spoken: Shechem, Gilead, Ephraim, and Judah are his. Moab, Edom, and Philistia are under him. Yet God has not gone out with their armies. With God they will still do bravely.
chapters.109.summary: The speaker asks God not to stay silent. Liars surround him and attack him without cause. They repay his love with accusation, and he prays. A long series of curses follows. The accused man should lose his office, his family, and his name. He never showed kindness and hunted the poor to death. The speaker is poor, weak from fasting, and mocked. He asks God to save him, for God stands beside the needy.
chapters.110.summary: The LORD tells the speaker’s lord to sit at his right hand. His enemies will become his footstool. The LORD will extend his rule from Zion. His people offer themselves freely on the day of battle. The LORD has sworn an oath and will not change it. This ruler is a priest forever, like Melchizedek. The Lord at his right hand will shatter kings. He will judge the nations and lift up his head.
chapters.111.summary: The speaker will thank the LORD with his whole heart among the upright. The LORD’s works are great and are studied by all who enjoy them. He is gracious and merciful. He gives food to those who fear him and remembers his covenant. He gave his people the lands of other nations. His commands are trustworthy and lasting. He sent redemption to his people. The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.
chapters.112.summary: The poem blesses the person who fears the LORD and delights in his commands. His children will be strong, and his house will have wealth. Light rises in the dark for the upright. He is gracious, lends freely, and runs his affairs justly. He will not be shaken or fear bad news. His heart is steady. He gives freely to the poor. The wicked see it, are angry, and melt away.
chapters.113.summary: The poem calls the LORD’s servants to praise his name. His name is to be praised from sunrise to sunset. The LORD is high above all nations. No one is like him, seated on high. He stoops to look at the heavens and the earth. He raises the poor from the dust and the needy from the ash heap. He seats them with princes. He gives the childless woman a home and makes her a joyful mother.
chapters.114.summary: Israel went out of Egypt, from a people of foreign speech. Judah became God’s sanctuary. The sea saw it and fled, and the Jordan turned back. The mountains skipped like rams and the hills like lambs. The poet asks the sea and the river why they ran. He asks the mountains why they skipped. The earth should tremble before the God of Jacob. He turned the rock into a pool of water.
chapters.115.summary: The people ask that glory go to the LORD’s name and not to them. The nations ask where their God is. He is in the heavens and does whatever he pleases. The nations’ idols are silver and gold, made by human hands. They have mouths, eyes, ears, and hands that do nothing. Those who make them will become like them. Israel should trust the LORD, their help and shield. He will bless those who fear him, small and great.
chapters.116.summary: The speaker loves the LORD, who heard his cry. The cords of death had wrapped around him. He called on the LORD’s name and was saved. God rescued his life from death, his eyes from tears, and his feet from falling. He asks what he can give back to the LORD. He will lift the cup of salvation and call on the LORD’s name. He will keep his vows before all the people. He will offer thanks in the courts of the LORD’s house.
chapters.117.summary: This is the shortest psalm. It calls all nations to praise the LORD. It calls all peoples to honor him. The reason is that his kindness toward us is great. His faithfulness lasts forever.
chapters.118.summary: The people give thanks, for the LORD’s kindness lasts forever. The speaker called in distress, and the LORD set him free. Nations surrounded him like bees, and he cut them off in the LORD’s name. He was pushed hard and nearly fell. He will not die but live and tell what the LORD has done. He asks for the gates to be opened. The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. The people bless the one who comes in the LORD’s name.
chapters.119.summary: This is the longest psalm. It has twenty-two sections, one for each letter of the Hebrew alphabet. Almost every verse names God’s teaching as law, word, statute, or command. The speaker is young and feels like a stranger on the earth. Princes slander him, and he has suffered. He says God’s word is a lamp for his feet. He loves the commands more than gold. He ends by saying he has strayed like a lost sheep.
chapters.120.summary: This is the first of fifteen songs of ascents. The speaker cried to the LORD in distress and was answered. He asks to be saved from lying lips. He asks what a deceitful tongue deserves: sharp arrows and burning coals. He grieves that he lives in Meshech and among the tents of Kedar. He has lived too long with people who hate peace. He is for peace. When he speaks, they are for war.
chapters.121.summary: The speaker lifts his eyes to the hills and asks where his help comes from. It comes from the LORD, who made heaven and earth. God will not let his foot slip. The one who keeps Israel does not slumber or sleep. The LORD is his keeper and his shade. The sun will not harm him by day or the moon by night. The LORD will keep him from all evil. He will guard his going out and coming in forever.
chapters.122.summary: The speaker was glad when people said, “Let’s go to the LORD’s house.” Now his feet stand inside Jerusalem’s gates. The city is built firmly together. The tribes go up there to give thanks to the LORD. Thrones for judgment stand there, the thrones of David’s house. He calls for prayer for Jerusalem’s peace. He wishes peace within its walls. He seeks its good for the sake of his family and the LORD’s house.
chapters.123.summary: The speaker lifts his eyes to the one enthroned in heaven. Servants watch the hand of their master. A maid watches the hand of her mistress. In the same way the people watch the LORD until he shows mercy. They ask for mercy twice. They have had more than enough contempt. They are worn out by the scorn of the comfortable and the proud.
chapters.124.summary: The people say what would have happened without the LORD on their side. When men attacked, they would have been swallowed alive. The flood would have swept over them. The raging waters would have gone over their heads. They bless the LORD, who did not give them to those teeth. They escaped like a bird from a hunter’s trap. The trap broke. Their help is in the name of the LORD, who made heaven and earth.
chapters.125.summary: Those who trust the LORD are like Mount Zion, which cannot be moved. Mountains surround Jerusalem. In the same way the LORD surrounds his people now and forever. Wicked rule will not stay over the land of the righteous. Otherwise the righteous might turn to doing wrong. The poet asks the LORD to do good to the good. Those who turn to crooked ways will be led away. Peace be on Israel.
chapters.126.summary: When the LORD brought back Zion’s captives, the people were like dreamers. Their mouths were full of laughter and song. The nations said the LORD had done great things for them. The people agree and are glad. They ask the LORD to restore them again like streams in the Negev. Those who sow in tears will reap with joy. The one who goes out weeping with seed will return with sheaves.
chapters.127.summary: Unless the LORD builds the house, its builders work for nothing. Unless the LORD guards the city, the guard stays awake for nothing. It is useless to rise early and stay up late in anxious toil. God gives sleep to those he loves. Children are a gift from the LORD. They are like arrows in a warrior’s hand. The man with many is blessed. They will stand with him against enemies at the gate.
chapters.128.summary: Everyone who fears the LORD and walks in his ways is blessed. He will eat what his own hands have worked for. His wife will be like a fruitful vine in his house. His children will be like olive shoots around his table. The poem asks the LORD to bless him from Zion. May he see Jerusalem’s good all his life. May he see his children’s children. Peace be on Israel.
chapters.129.summary: Israel says it has been attacked many times since its youth. Yet its enemies have not won. Plowmen plowed its back and made their furrows long. The LORD is just and has cut the cords of the wicked. May all who hate Zion be turned back. May they be like grass on a roof that withers before it grows. No reaper fills his hands with it. No passerby gives it a blessing.
chapters.130.summary: The speaker cries to the LORD out of the depths. He asks the Lord to hear his voice. If God kept a record of sins, no one could stand. But with God there is forgiveness. The speaker waits for the LORD and hopes in his word. He waits more than watchmen wait for the morning. He tells Israel to hope in the LORD. With him is kindness and full redemption.
chapters.131.summary: The speaker tells the LORD that his heart is not proud. His eyes are not raised too high. He does not busy himself with matters too great for him. He has calmed and quieted his soul. His soul is like a weaned child with its mother. He tells Israel to hope in the LORD now and forever.
chapters.132.summary: The poem asks the LORD to remember David and his hardships. David swore not to rest until he found a place for the LORD. The people heard of the ark and went to worship at his footstool. They ask the LORD to arise and come to his resting place. The LORD swore that David’s sons would sit on his throne. The LORD has chosen Zion for his home. He will bless her food and satisfy her poor with bread. He will make David’s strength grow there.
chapters.133.summary: The poem says how good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in unity. It is like fine oil poured on the head. The oil runs down Aaron’s beard to the collar of his robes. It is like the dew of Mount Hermon falling on the hills of Zion. There the LORD commands his blessing. That blessing is life forever.
chapters.134.summary: This is the last of the songs of ascents. It calls the LORD’s servants to bless him. They stand in the LORD’s house by night. They are told to lift their hands toward the holy place. Then a blessing is spoken in return. May the LORD, who made heaven and earth, bless you from Zion.
chapters.135.summary: The poem calls the LORD’s servants to praise his name. He chose Jacob for himself. He does whatever he pleases in heaven, earth, and sea. He brings clouds, lightning, and wind. He struck Egypt’s firstborn and defeated great kings. He gave their land to Israel. The idols of the nations are silver and gold, made by hands. Israel, Aaron’s house, and Levi’s house are called to bless the LORD.
chapters.136.summary: The poem calls the people to thank the LORD, for he is good. Every line ends with “for his loving kindness endures forever.” He alone does great wonders. He made the heavens, the earth, the sun, and the moon. He brought Israel out of Egypt and divided the Red Sea. He led his people through the desert and struck down kings. He remembered them when they were low. He gives food to every creature.
chapters.137.summary: The exiles sat by the rivers of Babylon and wept for Zion. They hung their harps on the trees. Their captors asked them for a song of Zion. They ask how they can sing the LORD’s song in a foreign land. The speaker swears never to forget Jerusalem. He asks the LORD to remember what Edom said when the city fell. He speaks of Babylon’s coming ruin. The poem ends with fierce words about repayment.
chapters.138.summary: The speaker thanks the LORD with his whole heart. He sings praise before the “gods” and bows toward the holy temple. On the day he called, God answered and gave him strength. All the kings of the earth will thank the LORD. The LORD is high, yet he looks after the lowly. He knows the proud from far away. He keeps the speaker alive in trouble. The speaker asks him not to abandon the work of his hands.
chapters.139.summary: The LORD has searched the speaker and knows him. He knows when he sits and rises and what he will say. The speaker cannot flee from God’s Spirit. In heaven, in the grave, or across the sea, God’s hand holds him. Darkness is as light to God. God formed him in his mother’s womb. All his days were written before one of them came. He asks God to search his heart and lead him.
chapters.140.summary: The speaker asks the LORD to rescue him from evil and violent men. They plan harm and stir up strife all day. Their tongues are sharp like a serpent’s. The proud have hidden traps and nets for him. He says the LORD is his God and covers his head in battle. He asks that their own words bring them down. He knows the LORD upholds the cause of the poor. The upright will live in God’s presence.
chapters.141.summary: The speaker calls on the LORD to come quickly. He asks that his prayer rise like incense. He asks God to set a guard over his mouth. He asks that his heart not lean toward evil. He does not want to share the feasts of wrongdoers. He would welcome a good person’s rebuke as a kindness. His eyes are fixed on the LORD. He asks to be kept from the traps set for him.
chapters.142.summary: The heading sets this prayer in the cave where David hid. The speaker cries aloud and pours out his complaint. When his spirit is faint, God knows his path. Enemies have hidden a trap on the road. He looks to his right, and no one is there. No one cares about his life. He cries that the LORD is his refuge. He asks to be brought out of prison, and the righteous will gather around him.
chapters.143.summary: The speaker asks the LORD to hear him and answer in faithfulness. He asks God not to bring him to judgment. No one living is righteous before God. An enemy has crushed his life and made him sit in darkness. He remembers the days of old and stretches out his hands. His soul thirsts like dry ground. He asks to hear of God’s kindness in the morning. He asks to be taught the way to go.
chapters.144.summary: The speaker blesses the LORD, his rock, who trains his hands for battle. He asks what a human is, a breath and a passing shadow. He asks God to bend the heavens and come down. He asks rescue from foreigners whose mouths speak lies. He will sing a new song on the ten-stringed lyre. Then sons will grow like strong plants and daughters like carved pillars. Barns will be full and flocks many. No cry of distress will be heard in the streets.
chapters.145.summary: The speaker will praise God his King every day. One generation will tell the next of God’s mighty acts. The LORD is gracious, merciful, and slow to anger. He is good to all. His kingdom lasts through all generations. He holds up all who fall. Every creature looks to him for food at the right time. He is near to all who call on him in truth.
chapters.146.summary: The speaker will praise the LORD as long as he lives. He warns against trusting in princes. A human ruler dies, and his plans die that day. The one whose help is the God of Jacob is blessed. God made heaven, earth, and sea and keeps faith forever. He gives justice to the oppressed and food to the hungry. He frees prisoners and opens blind eyes. He guards foreigners, orphans, and widows.
chapters.147.summary: It is good to sing praise to the LORD. He builds up Jerusalem and gathers Israel’s outcasts. He heals the brokenhearted and binds their wounds. He counts the stars and names each one. He covers the sky with clouds and feeds animals and young ravens. He takes no pleasure in a horse’s strength. He sends snow, frost, and hail, and his word melts them. He has given his word to Israel.
chapters.148.summary: The poem calls for praise from the heavens. Angels, sun, moon, and stars are told to praise the LORD. He commanded, and they were created. Then it calls for praise from the earth. Sea creatures, fire, hail, snow, and wind are named. Mountains, trees, wild animals, cattle, and birds follow. Kings and all peoples are called, young and old. The LORD’s name alone is exalted.
chapters.149.summary: The poem calls for a new song in the gathering of the faithful. Israel should rejoice in its Maker. The people praise with dancing, tambourine, and lyre. The LORD takes pleasure in his people and honors the humble with victory. The faithful sing for joy on their beds. Praise is in their mouths and a two-edged sword in their hands. They are to carry out the judgment that is written. This is the honor of all his faithful ones.
chapters.150.summary: The last psalm calls for praise to God in his sanctuary and in the heavens. He is to be praised for his mighty acts and his greatness. Praise him with trumpet, harp, and lyre. Praise him with tambourine and dancing. Praise him with strings, pipe, and loud cymbals. Let everything that has breath praise the LORD.
